title.en: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe

text.en: Imagine a map where your country does not exist yet, only dozens of small kingdoms. In the 1800s that was the map of Germany and Italy. Today we see how people came to feel they belonged to one nation.

In 1848 the French artist Frederic Sorrieu painted a dream of democratic and social republics, with people of Europe marching in groups with their national flags.
The French Revolution of 1789 introduced ideas of la patrie, the citizen, a tricolour flag and an elected National Assembly. The idea of a nation of equal citizens spread.
Napoleon brought the Civil Code of 1804, also called the Napoleonic Code, which ended privileges by birth and made laws equal. It also removed customs barriers.
After Napoleon's defeat, European powers met at Vienna in 1815 and restored conservative rule. Liberal nationalists wanted a constitution, freedom of the press and free markets.
Giuseppe Mazzini founded Young Italy in Marseilles and Young Europe in Berne. Revolutionaries in 1830 and 1848 pushed for national unity.
Germany was united under Prussia, led by Otto von Bismarck and the army, in 1871. Wilhelm I was proclaimed German emperor at Versailles.
Italy was united through Cavour, Garibaldi's Red Shirts and the House of Sardinia-Piedmont under Victor Emmanuel II, who became king of united Italy in 1861.
In the Balkans, nationalist tensions and great-power rivalry made the region explosive and helped lead to the First World War.

problem.en: Germany was united in 1871. How many years after the Treaty of Vienna (1815) was that?

prompt.en: Explain how nationalism led to the unification of Italy.

requiredIdeas.en: Italy was divided into several states
Mazzini, Cavour and Garibaldi worked in different ways
Sardinia-Piedmont's king became king of Italy

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking Italy was united by a single battle

points.en: The French Revolution spread ideas of nation and citizen.
Napoleon's Code made laws equal but rule was imposed.
The Balkans were a source of conflict.
